subject: sociology

items.correct: Judging other cultures by the standards of one's own — assuming one's own cultural practices and values are normal or superior. It is a methodological problem in social research as well as a social phenomenon.
items.misconception: Ethnocentrism is the same as racism.
items.random_wrong: Ethnocentrism means concentrating on your own ethnic group only.
items.why: Ethnocentrism involves judgement using one's own framework, while racism asserts inherent inferiority. Researchers may inadvertently be ethnocentric without being racist. Students treat the two as synonyms, missing the methodological dimension.

items.q: Which 1999 UK report defined institutional racism after the Stephen Lawrence murder?
items.why: Correct answer: Macpherson. “Scarman” sounds right because it borrows the language of the topic — but it fails this question. Re-read the notes on why.

items.q: Townsend's 1981 theory describing impoverishment by retirement is called what?
items.why: It's Structured dependency. “Liberation theology” is the classic near-miss here; knowing why it's wrong is worth as much as knowing the right answer.

items.q: In what year was the Macpherson Report published?
items.why: The real figure is 1999. The wrong options cluster deliberately close — anchor the exact number to one concrete fact so it can't drift.
